candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide preventive screening, health-promotion teaching, and age-appropriate family-centered care across pregnancy, postpartum, infancy, and childhood.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — postpartum depression screening during infant preventive care
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that postpartum depression screening is a routine, repeated component of early well-child care because timely identification and referral can support the birth parent, infant, and parent-infant relationship; a positive screen requires further assessment rather than serving as a diagnosis by itself.

options.A: Repeated screening during early well-child visits creates opportunities to identify postpartum depression and connect the parent with further evaluation, treatment, and support that can benefit the parent-infant dyad.
options.B: A positive screening score allows the pediatric team to make a definitive psychiatric diagnosis without further clinical evaluation.
options.C: Screening is needed only when the infant has feeding, growth, or developmental problems that already suggest parental depression.
options.D: Once screening is completed at the 2-month visit, additional postpartum depression screening during later early-infancy well visits is unnecessary.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends routine postpartum depression screening of the birth parent with a validated tool at the infant's 1-, 2-, 4-, and 6-month well-child visits. Repeated screening provides multiple opportunities to identify depression, initiate support, and arrange referral or treatment when indicated; perinatal depression can affect the parent, infant, and parent-infant relationship. B is incorrect because a screening result identifies risk and the need for further evaluation rather than establishing a psychiatric diagnosis by itself. C is incorrect because AAP recommends routine screening at specified well-child visits rather than waiting for infant problems or overt parental symptoms. D is incorrect because AAP specifically recommends repeated screening through the 6-month well-child visit.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AAP recommends routine repeated postpartum depression screening with a validated tool at 1-, 2-, 4-, and 6-month well-child visits to identify parents who may need further evaluation, treatment, referral, and support for the parent-infant dyad.
